extracted.intended_audience: vehicle manufacturers, safety stakeholders, and members of the public submitting comments to NHTSA docket for FMVSS No. 207
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for submitting public comments and related procedural/regulatory analyses for NHTSA's proposed rule to amend FMVSS No. 207 (Seating systems). Includes instructions on format, deadlines, confidential business information submissions, and the substantive proposed amendment to S4.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment language requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments must be written and in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated succinctly: 'Your comments must be written and in English.' No further language accommodation guidance provided on this page.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include agency name and docket number or RIN
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions must include the agency name and docket number or Regulatory Information Number (RIN) for this rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To ensure that comments are correctly filed in the Docket, include the docket number indicated in this document in your comments regardless of submission method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment length limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Your comments must not be more than 15 pages long (49 CFR 553.21).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limit is intended to encourage concise primary comments. You may attach necessary additional documents to your comments; there is no limit on the length of attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF submission OCR request
rubrics_metrics.description: If submitting comments electronically as a PDF (Adobe) file, NHTSA asks that the documents be submitted using the Optical Character Recognition (OCR) process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR allows NHTSA to search and copy portions of submissions. Follow online instructions when submitting via Regulations.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Quality Act standards for substantive data
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive data relied upon and used by the agency must meet the information quality standards set forth in the OMB and DOT Data Quality Act guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult OMB's and DOT's information quality guidelines when preparing comments; link provided to DOT guidance. This affects whether substantive data can be used by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to confirm docket receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If you wish the Docket to notify you upon its receipt of your comments, enclose a self-addressed, stamped postcard in the envelope containing your comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon receipt, the Docket will return the postcard by mail. This is the mechanism provided for confirmation of receipt for mailed submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment submission methods and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments may be submitted electronically at https://www.regulations.gov, by mail to Docket Management Facility (U.S. DOT address), by hand delivery/courier to the listed room and hours, or by fax to (202) 493-2251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the online instructions for submitting comments via Regulations.gov. For hand delivery, call (202) 366-9826 before coming to ensure assistance is available. Regardless of how you submit, mention the docket number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Business Information (CBI) submission procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If you claim information in your comment constitutes confidential business information, submit a redacted 'public version' to the docket and one unredacted 'confidential version' to the Office of Chief Counsel, following 49 CFR part 512.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your request for confidential treatment must set forth required information specified in part 512, include supporting information pursuant to §512.8, and include a certificate per §512.4(b) and part 512, appendix A. Label each page with either 'ENTIRE PAGE CONFIDENTIAL BUSINESS INFORMATION' or put bracketed markings '[ ]' around confidential items. NHTSA currently treats electronic submission as acceptable; do not send a hardcopy of a request for confidential treatment to NHTSA headquarters. A courtesy copy to John Piazza is requested. You may submit the request via email or request a secure file transfer link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Posting of comments and Privacy Act notice
rubrics_metrics.description: All comments received will be posted without change to https://www.regulations.gov, including any personal information provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DOT solicits comments in accordance with 5 U.S.C. 553(c) and posts comments for public viewing. Providing your name or organization is optional. Review DOT's Privacy Act Statement (DOT/ALL-14 FDMS) for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of late comments
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA will consider all comments received before the close of business on the comment closing date; to the extent possible, it will also consider comments received after that date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a comment is received too late to be considered in developing a final rule, it may be considered as an informal suggestion for future rulemaking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to docket materials and comments
rubrics_metrics.description: You may access the docket to read background documents or comments online at Regulations.gov or at the physical docket location and hours listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow online instructions for accessing the docket. The agency will continue to file relevant information in the docket as it becomes available even after the comment closing date; users are recommended to check periodically and may arrange to be notified when others file comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: NHTSA rule objective and scope (removal of obsolete requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA proposes to remove obsolete requirements from FMVSS No. 207, Seating systems. The requirement in S4.2 applies to passenger seats on school buses manufactured before October 21, 2011, and therefore is obsolete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NHTSA seeks comment on all aspects of this proposal. This action does not affect the applicability of 49 U.S.C. 30122, which prohibits making inoperative any device or element of design installed pursuant to an FMVSS applicable on the date of manufacture.

rubrics_metrics.name: FMVSS S4.2 general performance requirement (seat strength)
rubrics_metrics.description: When tested in accordance with S5, each occupant seat shall withstand the following forces, in newtons, except for: a side-facing seat; a passenger seat on a bus other than a school bus; and, a passenger seat on a school bus with a GVWR greater than 4,536 kilograms (10,000 pounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the revised introductory text of S4.2 as proposed; the requirement is enforceable when tests are performed per S5. (The specific force values are referenced in the standard's text elsewhere.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Flexibility Act (RFA) certification
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA certifies that this proposed rule will not have a significant economic impact on a substantial number of small entities; therefore, a regulatory flexibility analysis is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The certification is based on the agency's conclusion that the proposed rule will only remove directives that are no longer needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unfunded Mandates Reform Act (UMRA) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule does not contain Federal mandates for State, local and Tribal governments, or the private sector of $100 million or more in any one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because it does not meet the UMRA threshold, the rulemaking is not subject to sections 202 and 205 of UMRA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tribal implications / Executive Order 13175
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA has assessed the impact of this proposed rule on Indian tribes and determined that it would not have tribal implications that require consultation under Executive Order 13175.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must consult with Tribes on policies with substantial direct effects on Indian Tribes; NHTSA concluded consultation is not required for this deregulatory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paperwork Reduction Act statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, an agency may not conduct or sponsor, and a person is not required to respond to, a collection of information unless it displays a currently valid OMB control number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proposed deregulatory rule would not impose any additional information collection requirements. Comments on the proposed information collection requirements should also be submitted to OMB via reginfo.gov (Currently under Review—Open for Public Comment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Order 12866/13563 significant regulatory action determination
rubrics_metrics.description: This proposed rule does not meet the criteria of a 'significant regulatory action' under Executive Order 12866, as amended by Executive Orders 14215 and 13563; therefore, OMB has not reviewed this proposed rule under those orders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement notifies readers that the rule is not designated as significant for interagency review under EO 12866.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preemption and Federalism considerations (EO 13132 and 49 U.S.C. 30103)
rubrics_metrics.description: NHTSA examined whether this proposed rule could or should preempt State common law causes of action and concluded it does not intend this proposed rule to preempt state tort law that would effectively impose a higher standard than that established by this proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains express preemption under 49 U.S.C. 30103(b)(1), the savings clause under 30103(e), and the possibility of implied preemption only where an actual conflict exists. NHTSA reviewed the regulatory text and objectives and does not foresee potential State requirements that might conflict with the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plain language solicitation and criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying plain language principles, the agency asks commenters to consider: Have we organized the material to suit the public's needs? Are the requirements in the rule clearly stated? Does the rule contain technical language or jargon that isn't clear? Would a different format (grouping and order of sections, use of headings, paragraphing) make the rule easier to understand? Would more (but shorter) sections be better? Could we improve clarity by adding tables, lists, or diagrams? What else could we do to make the rule easier to understand?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have any responses to these questions, include them in your comments on this proposal. These are criteria the agency will use to evaluate suggestions for clearer rule text and presentation.
